transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Start: 10:30 AM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Raj (ParcelWorks CTO), Dana (ML infra), Samir (Platform), Lena (Security)

Summary:
Quick mid-week POC sync focused on onboarding progress, VPC/access gating, and readiness to run the first baseline benchmark. Agreed next steps above; sequencing of network -> creds -> benchmark clarified. Some discussion about dedicated vs hosted fallbacks and security paperwork (SOC2 / KMS).

Topics: onboarding checklist; VPC peering; SSO/SAML; QPS/latency targets; canary/rollout; logs/audit; benchmark timing

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Aisha (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call — we have Aisha, Marco and Jordan from Redwood, and Raj, Dana, Samir, Lena from ParcelWorks. Are we good to start?
[00:18] Raj (ParcelWorks): Yep, yep, go ahead. A couple minutes delayed, sorry.
[00:22] Marco (Redwood): No worries. Today's agenda: access and network readiness, creds and SSO, and then confirm the benchmark window. We'll also surface any blockers for the POC entrance gate.
[00:33] Dana (ParcelWorks): Sounds good. We mostly want to get the env ramped and make sure keys and traffic path are set. We've got a constrained maintenance window next week, so timing matters.
[01:05] Jordan (Redwood): Quick callout — we've uploaded the onboarding runbook link in the deck chat; it's the one with the step-by-step for peering, S3, and the test harness.
[01:22] Raj: I saw that, but the network diagram looked like a couple of the subnets were placeholders. Can you confirm NAT IPs and exact cidrs so our infra team can schedule the peering change?
[01:38] Aisha: Yes we'll attach a finalized VPC diagram after this meeting. Marco will own the diagram update.
[01:45] Marco: I'll do that, and include the firewall rules. One thing to mention: there's a required egress nat IP list for the Redwood edge nodes, and also TLS client cert details if you opt in for mTLS.
[02:10] Samir (ParcelWorks): Regarding mTLS — we prefer to stick with SAML/SSO for the service account flows; mTLS is extra work for the network team. Is it a hard requirement?
[02:26] Marco: No, not hard; mTLS is optional for extra security. For the pilot we can use standard TLS + customer-managed KMS for keys. If you later want HSM integration we can scope it.
[02:55] Lena (Security): For compliance we need explicit audit log retention details and an outline of encryption at rest. Is that in the docs?
[03:10] Jordan: Yep, there's a security appendix in the runbook. High-level: SOC2 controls, KMS integration, and audit logs. I'll re-share the security PDF and mark the specific sections (audit retention and rotation).
[03:42] Raj: Great. On the latency targets — our SLAs for the service are 200ms p95 for short responses, and we want to see baseline numbers to evaluate. Any rough numbers from similar customers?
[03:58] Marco: For a small single-token generation (50 tokens) on our hosted inferencers we typically see 60–120ms p95, depending on model and sequence length and batching. On Dedicated it can be lower and more predictable. But key is the warm KV cache and continuous batching profile.
[04:35] Dana: Hmm ok. We will plan a realistic profile — a mix of short and medium responses. We'll share the corpus.
[04:46] Aisha: Perfect. Next: creds. We need to provision service account access. Samir, can you confirm where you want the creds stored — S3 vs internal vault?
[04:58] Samir: Internal vault — HashiVault. We'll create a dynamic secret role if possible. How do we do the handshake?
[05:12] Marco: We'll provide a presigned S3 template and also a small script that writes into Vault. Aisha will send the template today.
[05:26] Aisha: I'll send that after the call.
[05:30] Raj: On the test corpus — do you have any constraints about PII or doc formats?
[05:39] Marco: Keep PII out of the test set; PDFs and JSON are fine. We'll run inference against the same payload you intend to use in production, so format matters.
[05:55] Dana: Understood. We'll scrub and send 5k docs by Tuesday.
[06:06] Lena: Are logs written to a customer-controlled bucket or to Redwood storage? We need to ensure logs don't persist beyond the retention window.
[06:18] Jordan: For the POC we can ship logs to your S3 or to Redwood with explicit retention. We'll prefer S3 if you want full control.
[06:30] Samir: We'll accept S3. Make sure the log schema includes trace IDs so we can map requests.
[06:38] Marco: Yes, trace IDs and token/audio-level timings are included. There's a small caveat: token-level timing can be noisy in the transcribed logs, sometimes misaligned.
[07:02] Raj: Good to know.
[07:08] Aisha: OK next big question — are you leaning Dedicated vs Hosted for this pilot? That affects the ramp and peering details.
[07:18] Raj: For the trial, we prefer hosted for speed of setup, but if Dedicated can be available for testing of higher QPS soon, we'd like to evaluate that too. Cost will be a factor.
[07:33] Marco: Totally. Hosted will be fastest — we just need SSO and S3 creds. Dedicated needs reserved capacity and a slightly longer provisioning lead time. We can run the same benchmark on both for apples-to-apples.
[07:50] Dana: About fallback — can requests automatically route to a smaller model or a different region if capacity constrained? We need graceful degradation.
[08:03] Marco: Yes, we have smart routing and fallback policies. For POC we can set a simple fallback policy: when p95 exceeds X, route to a lower-cost model. We'll show the config snippet in the runbook.
[08:22] Lena: Do you support customer-managed KMS keys for encrypting model caches? Our compliance team wants key ownership.
[08:33] Marco: Yes you can bring your own KMS for at-rest encryption. HSM is also supported on Private deployments but that would need additional scoping.
[08:48] Raj: Fine. Any open blockers on our side? Samir?
[08:54] Samir: Network team is waiting on the exact NAT IP list and the peering steps. Also need confirmation on egress ports — we'll need port 443 plus some healthcheck ports.
[09:08] Aisha: We'll provide the NAT IP list and the minimal firewall rules.
[09:14] Marco: I'll include ports and a snippet for security groups.
[09:20] Raj: Great.
[09:24] [10:00] Jordan: Quick note on metrics — we'll enable cost-per-token breakdown and per-route latency in the console for the POC so you can see unit economics. That data can be exported.
[10:35] Dana: That's useful. We'll want token-level cost to compare quantized model performance later.
[10:45] Marco: Speaking of quantization — if you want to run a quantized variant to reduce cost, we'll need to measure quality regressions. We have an eval harness but we'll need labeled prompt sets.
[11:02] Raj: We can provide labeled sets but that's after the baseline. Baseline first.
[11:10] Aisha: Timeline check — we propose: today finalize diagram; by Mon/Tue have creds and corpus; by Wed run baseline smoke; benchmark week of 3/29 for heavier runs. Does that align with your maintenance window?
[11:26] Samir: Yes, that fits. Maintenance window starts Friday evening so baseline should be okay if we run during the day.
[11:34] Lena: About the security questionnaire — Jordan, can you assign us a point-of-contact for SOC2 followups?
[11:42] Jordan: Sure, I'll loop in our security lead and copy you with the answers; expect an initial response in 48 hours.
[11:52] Raj: One more tech question — what's the expected tokenization differences? We had issues in a previous pilot where token counts were off so costs were higher.
[12:05] Marco: We'll share exact tokenizer versions used in the model config; that way you can pre-tokenize and estimate costs. Also caching behavior (prefix/KV cache) can reduce token spend if you have repeating prefixes.
[12:25] Dana: Good. We'll try to create repeatable sessions to take advantage of KV cache.
[12:34] Aisha: Anything else blocking?
[12:37] Raj: None from me.
[12:39] Samir: No.
[12:40] Lena: Just the SOC2 answers.
[12:42] Aisha: OK let's recap quickly.
[12:45] [31:00] Recap (Aisha): Redwood will: 1) share updated VPC peering diagram and firewall snippet (Marco) by 3/22, 2) send presigned S3 creds template and onboarding runbook (Aisha) today, 3) start baseline smoke tests once Samir confirms NAT IPs ~ by 3/25. ParcelWorks will: 1) provide scrubbed test corpus (Dana) by 3/24, 2) provide egress IPs and confirm peering (Samir) by 3/23, 3) review SOC2 questions (Lena) and confirm auditor contact.
[31:45] Jordan: I'll also enable the console telemetry for cost/latency and share the dashboard link.
[32:05] Raj: That sounds good. Any objections to scheduling the benchmark week of 3/29?
[32:10] Dana: No objections.
[32:13] Aisha: We'll send a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.
[32:18] Marco: One small note — expect occasional transcription mistakes in the logs, sometimes product names get scrambled (e.g., 'K-V cash' or 'Dedicate' vs Dedicated) — it's a known issue with auto captions.
[32:31] Raj: Ha, okay we'll forgive the captions.
[32:36] [39:00] Close: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the artifacts. Meeting adjourned.

Action items (in transcript):
- Aisha: send S3 template + runbook (today)
- Marco: update network diagram + firewall rules (3/22)
- Samir: provide NAT IPs and CIDRs (3/23)
